teaser: One researcher for every newsroom: research.newsroom.sgit.ai, a light, focused archive captured on a schedule into a pack a day.
core_idea: Instead of each newsroom running its own slow researcher over overlapping sources, one shared researcher should run scheduled, parallel captures of the daily web, Wikipedia and focus requests into a daily sgit pack with its provenance, publish them at research.newsroom.sgit.ai by licence tier, open pages in full and the rest as records, and let each team research only what is not covered.

quotes.text: The researcher already describes its source watch as "a small Wayback Machine for one story".
Most of what makes the archive useful, what changed, when, and who said it first, is in the record, not the bytes.

figures.caption: research.newsroom.sgit.ai, one researcher shared by every newsroom: a watch list of what to watch, who asked, how often and its licence tier; three kinds of scheduled run, the daily web, Wikipedia, and focus runs for current work; a pack a day in an sgit pack vault, with an index of what is inside; the research site, where tier A is published in full and tiers B and C as index, hashes and links; and the readers, the PHP story site, the Industry Wire, the Web Summit newsroom and anyone outside. Proposed.

Why pack mode makes this possible: the source watch vault measured by the PHP site's researcher on 23 October 2026, as a normal sgit vault and as a pack vault; a fresh clone took 827 seconds and 95 seconds, listing the vault on the server 91 seconds (a failure, HTTP 504) and 0.73 seconds, a pull with nothing new 34 seconds and 4 seconds; the vault was 1,614 MB as loose objects and 1,184 MB as packs.

What the research site may publish, by tier: tier A, open or public sector, the full capture in a public pack with a published read key, 73 of the source watch's pages, and Wikipedia under its open licence; tier B, at most 25 words and a link, the index, hash and change record in public and the full bytes in a private vault, 523 pages; tier C, link only, 15 pages. And an opt-out: any publisher who asks us to stop, we stop.
